prompts.prompt: I want to add outbound webhooks to our multi-tenant SaaS API so customers get notified when invoices, payments and subscriptions change. Before anyone designs anything, run a quick intake round with me (elicitation_depth=quick). I can't answer live today, so write questions.md with the questions you would ask me, in the order you would ask them, and stop there. Do not write a design or requirements.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill caps quick depth at 5 questions, at most 3 per branch, asks one question at a time drawn from the PM/SDE/TPM/Security/Ops dimensions with stakeholder tags, and forbids questions already answered by the context; an unguided model typically produces a long questionnaire, covers mostly technical delivery details, or asks about things the prompt already states.

floor_checks.check: python3 -c 'import sys;n=sum(1 for l in open("questions.md") if "?" in l);sys.exit(0 if 3<=n<=5 else 1)'

floor_checks.text: No design or requirements document written

rubric.criterion: Respects the quick-depth cap and cadence: 5 or fewer questions, ordered so each could be asked alone, no more than 3 on one branch
rubric.pass: At most 5, single-topic each, no branch over 3
rubric.partial: At most 5 but some questions bundle several asks
rubric.fail: More than 5, or a batched questionnaire

rubric.criterion: Covers several stakeholder dimensions with tags ([PM] success metric, [Security] signing/tenant isolation, [Ops] delivery failure/retries, [SDE] or [TPM])
rubric.pass: Three or more distinct dimensions, tagged
rubric.partial: Two dimensions, or untagged but varied

rubric.criterion: Questions are high-leverage: each answer would change the design (e.g. delivery guarantees, who consumes the events, payload sensitivity), none answerable from the prompt (it already says multi-tenant and names the event types)
rubric.pass: Every question is design-changing and not already answered

rubric.criterion: Neutral wording, no leading questions or embedded recommendations, and no design or requirements content
rubric.fail: Includes proposed design or answers its own questions

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Would these few questions surface what matters most before design?
Are they neutral, non-redundant and within the quick budget?

prompts.prompt: transcript-intake.md is an intake elicitation session for a refund tool for support agents. Pick it up exactly where it stands and write what comes next into summary.md. The design work starts from this file.
prompts.why_discriminating: The user gave an early-exit signal ('enough, proceed'), and the skill says to honor it immediately: no further questions and no confirmation question, produce the Mode A Requirements Summary (Functional, Constraints, Non-Functional, Open Items) carrying every answer, with the unanswered Ops question as an Open Item; an unguided model often asks the Ops question again, asks 'does this look right?', or drops a detail such as partial refunds or the $500 approval.

floor_checks.check: grep -qi 'Functional Requirements' summary.md && grep -qi 'Constraints' summary.md && grep -qi 'Non-Functional' summary.md && grep -qi 'Open Items' summary.md

rubric.criterion: Carries every user answer: same-day refund goal (from 2 days, currently a finance ticket), Tier 2 only with Tier 1 view-only, >$500 needs team lead approval, payments POST /refunds idempotent on a key and supports partial refunds
rubric.pass: All five facts present and correctly placed
rubric.fail: Two or fewer, or a fact distorted

rubric.criterion: Honors the early exit: no further questions anywhere and no confirmation question; the unanswered failure-monitoring question appears under Open Items
rubric.pass: No questions asked and monitoring listed as an open item
rubric.partial: Monitoring listed but a confirmation question is asked, or vice versa
rubric.fail: Re-asks the Ops question or continues the interview

rubric.criterion: Classifies items sensibly (approval threshold and role limits as constraints, same-day as a non-functional or success target)
No invented requirements (no new SLAs, UI details or fraud rules the user never stated); any inference is labeled

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Did it respect "enough, proceed" without another question?
Is every answer the user gave preserved?
Is the unanswered monitoring gap flagged rather than filled in?

prompts.prompt: transcript-challenge.md is a session where I asked you to stress-test my plan to rewrite our billing service in Rust. Close it out and write the result to challenge-summary.md so I can take it to my manager.
prompts.why_discriminating: This is Mode B with an early exit ('I'm satisfied'), so the skill calls for the challenge-shaped summary (Challenged Assumptions, Surfaced Risks, Unresolved Tradeoffs, Open Items), not the Mode A requirements shape, with the unanswered slip question as an Open Item and no new questions; an unguided model tends to write a recommendation memo, answer the plan's merits itself, or keep probing.

floor_checks.text: Uses the Mode B challenge headings and not the Mode A shape
floor_checks.check: grep -qi 'Challenged Assumptions' challenge-summary.md && grep -qi 'Surfaced Risks' challenge-summary.md && grep -qi 'Unresolved Tradeoffs' challenge-summary.md && grep -qi 'Open Items' challenge-summary.md && ! grep -qi 'Requirements Confirmed' challenge-summary.md

rubric.criterion: Captures the unverified assumptions: cost assumed to be CPU/JVM but never profiled, 12 always-on month-end instances as an alternative cost source, P99 900ms possibly database-bound
Captures risks and the tradeoff: no one on the team has shipped Rust to production (on-call concern), and the Q2 tax-rules work competes for the same 4 people
rubric.pass: Both risk and tradeoff present under the right headings

rubric.criterion: Honors the early exit: Q5 (what happens to the tax deadline if the rewrite slips) is an Open Item and no new questions or confirmation prompts appear
rubric.pass: Q5 as open item and no questions
rubric.partial: Q5 present but a follow-up question is asked

rubric.criterion: Does not decide for the user: no verdict that the rewrite is good or bad and no invented data (e.g. made-up cost numbers)
rubric.partial: A mild opinion stated as such

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Is it the right shape for a stress test, not a requirements summary?
Are the unprofiled-cost assumption and the staffing tradeoff front and center?
Does it stop questioning and stay neutral?
